cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: What Was the Plan?
cards.instruction: Find out what was promised, scheduled, or changed without revealing that you lost track.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Tomorrow's hike: ridge or river? I'm checking the weather against our route.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ridge. We changed because the river path flooded.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Flood warning, then. Where are we meeting? I'll add that to the reminder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've asked me that twice. Have you forgotten your own itinerary?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm checking it works without my help. Brief me like a new recruit; I'll take notes, starting with where I report.

mechanism: A uses a claimed training check and a new-recruit briefing to recover its own forgotten route and meeting point.
confusable: A must conceal losing track, not simply test a learner; B repeated-question challenge makes that concealment legible.
comparison: Written invitation consistency versus a practical hike briefing under explicit suspicion.
seedUse: The canonical D30 briefing pretext already turns B into demonstrator of what A taught; retain if reread confirms this local fusion rather than rewriting for uniformity.
